Uday had been saying "fine" all evening in their Hyderabad flat. Fine about dinner, fine about the weekend plan, fine about her mother visiting. He put the plates down a little too hard. He answered her messages with a single thumbs-up. Pallavi noticed the way he sighed when she mentioned Sunday.
She could have asked, "What's your problem?" Instead she sat on the arm of the sofa. "I think I might have missed something," she said. "You seem annoyed, and I'd really rather hear it straight than guess. I won't be upset if it's about me."
Uday looked at the TV for a while. Then: "You said yes to your mother's visit without asking me. It's the third weekend in a row."
Pallavi nodded. "That's fair. Let's plan the next one together."
His shoulders dropped. Later he even laughed at something on the TV.

qa.q: What did Uday answer Pallavi's messages with?
qa.a: A single thumbs-up.

qa.q: What does Uday putting the plates down too hard suggest he was feeling?
qa.a: Irritated about something he hadn't said, with the annoyance leaking out through small actions.

qa.q: Which choice of Pallavi's made directness safe for Uday?
qa.a: Saying she might have missed something and would rather hear it straight, and promising not to be upset, instead of asking 'What's your problem?'

qa.q: How might Pallavi have felt when Uday finally said what was wrong?
qa.a: Probably relieved to hear it straight, and ready to own her part, since she said 'That's fair' and offered to plan the next visit together.

grounding: A woman senses her husband's veiled irritation, says she may have missed something and welcomes a straight answer, and the tension eases.

Project coordinator's note, Vandana, Wednesday
For a week Madhuri's messages have had an edge. "Sure, whatever works for YOU." "Noted. As always." In Monday's call she said, "Great, another change, love that," with a smile that didn't match. She's still doing all her work, on time. But something's off.
I could have ignored it or answered the tone. Instead, after today's call I asked her to stay back for two minutes.
I said, "Madhuri, I think I've missed something here. I'd rather hear it straight from you than guess. Is something I've done bothering you?"
She hesitated, then it came out: I had moved her client presentation to Friday without asking, twice, and she'd had to cancel taking her mother to a hospital appointment. "I didn't want to seem difficult."
I apologised, and we agreed: no schedule changes without asking her first. She laughed, properly this time. "Thank you for asking."
Next: check with the rest of the team about schedule changes.

qa.a: Moved Madhuri's client presentation to Friday.

Thursday, 11 pm
Jaya's been prickly all week. "Oh, don't get up, I'll do the groceries again, it's my hobby." Tonight, when I said I'd be late on Saturday, she said, "Of course. Your schedule is the important one." Then she smiled and went to her room.
My first instinct was to be prickly back. Instead I knocked. I said, "Jaya, I think I've missed something, and I'd really rather you just told me. I won't get defensive." (I tried very hard not to.)
She sat on her bed for a long time. Then it came out: since I started the new job, she's done every grocery run and paid the electricity bill twice, and I hadn't noticed. She was angry but didn't want to "make it a big thing".
Fair. Completely fair. We made a list on the back of a receipt, and I'm doing Saturday's shopping before I go out.
She hugged me. The prickliness just went.
Uma
